newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian blue chips up in buoyant trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian blue chips up in buoyant trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in buoyant trade on Friday, with blue chips closing on a firmer note and traders expected the trend to be carried over into the next week.
"The market is in the phase of growth. Nothing spectacular will happen, but prices could forge ahead a bit," a trader said.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka accounted for most of the day's trading with 7,321 and 7,044 shares sold, respectively.

Pliva added six kuna to 485 after peaking at 489 kuna earlier in the session. The firm said earlier on Friday its 1996 net profit went up 14.39 percent to 456 million kuna, while pre-tax profit grew 30.9 percent to 616 million.
"After such good results, it is normal for Pliva to grow... and I expect it to post some new, though mild gains soon," the trader said.
But he maintained there wasn't "much room" for Zagrebacka to rise further after the bank led gainers on Friday, climbing 48.55 kuna or 2.4 percent to 2,060 kuna.

Six of 15 active issues rose on Friday, six fell and three were flat. Volume rose to 17,259 from 4,837 shares, and turnover was more than six times higher at 19.9 million kuna. Weekly turnover was slightly lower at 53.8 million kuna.

Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka's first issue sold only one share, falling 1,100 kuna to 44,900. Traders predicted new losses for the stock, unless the bank opts for a share-split at the annual shareholders meeting next week.
Food processor Podravka was the third most active issue with 3,723 units, inching down 1.50 kuna to 305.50.
Biggest decliner hotelier Jadranturist lost nine kuna to 305, with 115 units sold.
Hotel stocks Areanturist and Istraturist lost two kuna each to 140 and 203 kuna, respectively. Riviera was stable at 160 kuna.
Traders believe that the approaching summer season, expected to be fairly successful, would boost demand for tourist stocks.
